name: ACT
inputs: Multi-view RGB and joint state
architecture: Visual encoder and transformer CVAE
training: Action reconstruction plus KL regularization
data: Task-specific teleoperation demonstrations
inference: Zero latent at deployment; repeatedly predict chunks and combine overlapping predictions
contribution: Reduce effective imitation horizon on low-cost bimanual hardware
limitations: Limited demonstration support; no built-in language foundation model or guaranteed contact-force reasoning
openness: Code and hardware design available

name: Diffusion Policy
inputs: Recent visual observations and robot state
architecture: Conditional temporal diffusion network
training: Denoising / score learning on expert actions
data: Robot manipulation demonstration benchmarks
inference: Iterative denoising; execute a prefix and re-observe
contribution: Model multimodal action distributions with receding-horizon feedback
limitations: Sampling cost and data coverage remain limiting; original model is not automatically a web-pretrained VLA
openness: Code and training materials available

name: RT-1
inputs: Short image history and language instruction
architecture: EfficientNet with FiLM, TokenLearner, transformer
action_representation: Discretized arm/base controls and termination mode
training: Supervised action-token prediction
data: Over 130k episodes, over 700 tasks, 13 robots
inference: 3 Hz policy loop with termination condition
contribution: Demonstrated scalable multitask robot behavior cloning
limitations: Mostly restricted robot/task distribution; language conditioning is not equivalent to large VLM reasoning
openness: Code and data links public

name: RT-2
inputs: RGB and task text
architecture: Pretrained PaLI-X or PaLM-E adapted to robot control
action_representation: Robot action bins serialized as text tokens
training: Co-fine-tuning robot trajectories and web vision-language tasks
data: Robot actions plus web VLM corpora
inference: Autoregressively generate and detokenize actions, then re-observe
contribution: Transfer semantic web knowledge directly into action selection
limitations: New semantic concepts do not imply new low-level motor skills; large decoder adds latency
openness: Research report; complete trained model not openly reproduced

name: RT-X / Open X-Embodiment
inputs: Robot images and language across platforms
architecture: RT-1-X and RT-2-X retain their respective base architectures
action_representation: Standardized action interfaces with dataset-specific semantics
training: Multirobot supervised policy learning
data: Pooled data from 22 robot embodiments in initial report
inference: Decode to target robot interface within a feedback loop
contribution: Established positive transfer from heterogeneous robot experience
limitations: Common file schema does not ensure identical physics, control frequency, or coordinates
openness: Dataset/code resources; openness differs between RT variants

name: Octo
inputs: Language or goal image; flexible observation streams
architecture: Modular tokenizers, transformer and diffusion action head
action_representation: Continuous action chunks; replaceable action heads
training: Robot pretraining plus efficient domain fine-tuning
data: 800k Open X-Embodiment trajectories
inference: Sample action chunk, execute prefix, replan
contribution: Flexible sensors and action spaces without requiring a giant language decoder
limitations: Needs adaptation for new interfaces; robot pretraining does not by itself give broad conversational reasoning
openness: Open code and checkpoints

name: OpenVLA
inputs: Robot image and instruction
architecture: DINOv2/SigLIP visual features with Llama 2 language backbone
training: Action-token cross-entropy and optional efficient fine-tuning
data: 970k real robot demonstrations; 7B model
inference: Sequential action-token decoding and robot feedback
contribution: Accessible VLA pretraining and adaptation reference
limitations: Original decoder is expensive for high-frequency chunks; new hardware generally requires tuning
openness: Code and weights available; component licenses apply

name: OpenVLA-OFT
inputs: Images, instruction and configurable robot state
architecture: OpenVLA adapted for parallel chunk prediction
training: L1 regression with parallel decoding and chunking
data: Task-adaptation data; LIBERO and real ALOHA evaluations
inference: Predict multiple actions in parallel; update observations during control
contribution: Shows fine-tuning/output design can dominate practical speed and success
limitations: L1 favors a conditional median; multimodal behavior and language grounding need separate checks
openness: Code and checkpoints public

name: pi0
inputs: Multi-view images, text, proprioception and noisy actions

inference: Cache observation prefix; integrate action vector field and execute chunks
contribution: Combine semantic VLM features with continuous dexterous control
limitations: Base generality and specialist performance are different settings; dataset mixture is not fully open

inputs: Normalized continuous action chunks during tokenization; image/text at policy time

name: pi0.5 / knowledge insulation
inputs: Images, task/subtask text and robot state

name: pi0.6

inference: Condition on high advantage at execution; value learning improves next policy iteration
contribution: Improve both successful completions per hour and reliability

inference: Update memory and condition subsequent decisions on prior attempts

training: Adversarial imitation + RL; ASE additionally rewards informative skill latents.
data: Unstructured motion collections and simulated interactions.
inference: Task or latent selection feeds reactive motor policy.
contribution: AMP learns style from distributions; ASE makes that repertoire steerable and reusable.
limitations: Style realism is not task correctness; changing latent too abruptly can destabilize motion; simulated evaluation.
openness: Code available; motion-data licenses separate.

name: PHC
inputs: Simulated body state and target reference motion.
architecture: Progressive multiplicative control policy (PMCP) with capacity allocated to hard sequences and recovery.
action_representation: Motor targets for physically simulated humanoid.
training: RL tracking; progressive skill learning and fail-state recovery.
data: Large human motion databases, noisy reference poses and simulation.
inference: Track, recover from failure, resume without resetting environment.
contribution: Treats recovery as part of control rather than an external reset.
limitations: Avatar result; physical actuator and sensor transfer not established by original paper.
openness: Official implementation available.

name: Humanoid Transformer
inputs: Causal history of proprioceptive observations/actions and walking commands.
architecture: Autoregressive causal transformer controller.
action_representation: Future motor actions / desired joint commands.
training: Large-scale model-free RL in randomized simulation.
data: Simulation across terrain/dynamics; real-robot evaluation.
inference: Rolling history alters behavior without weight updates.
contribution: Uses temporal context for implicit dynamics adaptation.
limitations: Does not solve semantic planning, object manipulation or arbitrarily strong disturbances.
openness: Paper/project available; complete release scope not verified.

name: H2O / OmniH2O
inputs: Human pose from RGB/VR, sparse motion goals, robot proprioception.
architecture: H2O privileged feasibility filter; OmniH2O privileged RL teacher distilled to deployable student.
action_representation: Kinematic pose goals into whole-body tracking motor actions.
training: Retargeting, feasibility filtering, RL/domain randomization; student supervised distillation.
data: Human motion corpus; OmniH2O-6 robot demonstrations for learned upper-layer skills.
inference: Human or autonomous policy produces pose targets; student stabilizes robot continuously.
contribution: Universal pose interface separates goal generation from physical execution.
limitations: Teleoperation is not autonomous task competence; sparse goals and retargeting lose information.
openness: Project links code and OmniH2O data.

name: HumanPlus
inputs: Low level: body/hand reference and state. High level: egocentric vision.
architecture: RL shadowing controller plus supervised visual skill policy.
action_representation: Whole-body and hand targets for a 33-DoF humanoid.
training: Human-motion RL pretraining; shadowing collects robot data; behavior cloning learns autonomy.
data: 40-hour human-motion data; up to 40 task demonstrations in reported experiments.
inference: Visual policy proposes commands; low-level controller executes with body feedback.
contribution: Closes the data-collection loop from humans to real robot learning.
limitations: Limited task/robot distribution; human imitation cannot directly infer all contact dynamics.
openness: Code, datasets and hardware references linked.

name: MaskedMimic
inputs: Partial future joints, trajectory, scene and/or text conditions.
architecture: Fully constrained tracking teacher; conditional-VAE partial-goal policy via motion inpainting.
action_representation: Physical-controller actions conditioned on sampled latent motion.
training: RL tracking followed by learning a partially constrained policy with randomized masks.
data: Motion data and simulated physical interaction.
inference: Infer missing movement consistent with constraints, act, observe and repeat.
contribution: Unifies control modalities by representing them as missing motion information.
limitations: Mostly simulated character evidence; ambiguous constraints and real hardware transfer remain gaps.
openness: Official NVIDIA project links code.

name: SONIC / GEAR-SONIC
inputs: Proprioception plus robot, human or hybrid reference motion.
architecture: Specialized encoders -> FSQ universal token -> shared control decoder; auxiliary motion decoder.
action_representation: Desired joint positions -> PD controllers; released policy runs at 50 Hz.
training: PPO tracking + reconstruction; domain randomization; runtime kinematic planner.
data: Original paper: 700-hour motion collection; current release also offers separate public data.
inference: VLA/VR/planner produces motion command; token policy and PD loop execute.
contribution: Explicit bridge between VLA semantic actions and low-level motor control; released variants improve deployment.
limitations: One-task VLA PoC is not broad autonomy; lookahead differs from latency; proprietary original corpus; preprint compute inconsistency omitted.
openness: Training/deployment code and checkpoints released; code/weights have different licenses.

name: ViNT
inputs: Recent RGB observations and visual goal token.
architecture: Visual encoders and transformer; replaceable goal representation.
action_representation: Normalized local waypoint trajectory and distance-to-goal estimate.
training: Goal-reaching supervised learning on diverse trajectories.
data: Hundreds of hours from multiple navigation platforms.
inference: Topological/global planner selects subgoal; local policy proposes waypoints; robot controller follows.
contribution: Reusable navigation affordances and adaptable task tokens.
limitations: Long range depends on planner and mapping; not a semantic manipulator or balance controller.
openness: Official code/checkpoints and deployment examples.

name: NoMaD
inputs: RGB history and optionally masked goal image.
architecture: ViNT context encoder conditions diffusion action decoder.
training: Diffusion behavior learning with goal masking.
data: Multi-robot navigation trajectories.
inference: Sample feasible-looking candidate path; execute segment; update observations and topological planner.
contribution: Represents alternative routes with a common exploration/navigation model.
limitations: Sampling latency and planner integration matter; no formal collision guarantee.
openness: Official code/checkpoints shared with ViNT.

name: GOAT
inputs: RGB-D/state and multimodal goal; persistent object memory.
architecture: Perception, instance-aware semantic mapping, matching and navigation planner.
action_representation: Goal locations and navigation commands through a robot-specific controller.
training: Pretrained perception modules; map/instance accumulation during deployment.
data: Real indoor environments; evaluated in nine homes.
inference: Update memory -> match known goal or explore -> navigate -> retain evidence.
contribution: Improvement comes from remembered environment state without retraining a universal action model.
limitations: Mapping/perception errors persist; system-level benchmark differs from end-to-end VLA tests.
openness: Paper/system project; GOAT-Bench has separate code/data.

name: Helix / Helix 02
inputs: Language, head/palm cameras, touch and full-body proprioception in Helix 02.
architecture: S2 semantic latents -> S1 transformer joint targets at 200 Hz -> S0 10M controller at 1 kHz.
action_representation: Joint targets followed by joint-level actuator commands.
training: Helix learned visuomotor control; Helix 02 S0 uses randomized simulation RL and human motion tracking.
data: S0: over 1,000 hours retargeted motion; complete S1/S2 corpus undisclosed.
inference: Multi-rate hierarchy preserves fast balance feedback while slow semantics updates goals.
contribution: Extends upper-body Helix to demonstrated full-body room-scale tasks.
limitations: Vendor demonstration; failure/intervention distribution, full training recipe and independent evaluation unavailable.
openness: Proprietary model; public technical descriptions.

name: Skild Brain / S1
inputs: Body/sensor context; S1 accepts a demonstration video with live observations.
architecture: Shared cross-embodiment model; precise layer structure/action decoder undisclosed.
action_representation: Robot actions; exact shared action parameterization undisclosed.
training: Cross-embodiment training; S1 episodic demonstration-conditioned pretraining.
data: Simulation and diverse physical data; complete data mixture not disclosed.
inference: Condition execution on example and ongoing context; new task need not update weights in reported ICL setting.
contribution: Task specification shifts toward demonstration and reusable physical knowledge.
limitations: Manufacturer evidence; unpublished architecture/weights and nonpublic splits prevent complete reproduction.
openness: Closed; commercial/partner access.

name: GO-1 / GO-1 Air
inputs: Multi-view images, instruction, proprioception
architecture: VLM plus latent-action planner plus diffusion action expert; Air removes planner
action_representation: Discrete latent plan; continuous action chunks
training: Latent action reconstruction/prediction followed by robot action denoising
data: Human video, cross-embodiment robot data and AgiBot World
inference: Predict latent plan then denoise action chunk and execute with feedback
contribution: Separates transfer of video motion knowledge from embodiment-specific continuous execution
limitations: Latent plan quality, embodiment alignment, data concentration and task-limited results
openness: Code and listed checkpoints/dataset releases; exact training reproducibility must be audited

name: SERL
inputs: Visual observation, robot state and reward
architecture: Off-policy actor-critic training and robot learning infrastructure
training: Sample-efficient real-world RL with prior demonstrations or experience
data: On-robot interaction and optional demonstrations
inference: Learned actor executes within the robot control stack
contribution: Operationalizes efficient online policy improvement
limitations: Reward/reset design and interaction burden; not one universal pretrained model
openness: Research software suite

name: HIL-SERL
inputs: Images, state, learned success reward and human corrections
architecture: Reward classifier, demonstration/replay buffers, actor-learner loop
action_representation: Continuous control through task-specific robot interface
training: Reward learning from positives/negatives, demonstrations and online off-policy RL with interventions
data: Task-specific demonstrations, success labels and online interventions
inference: Actor controls robot; human corrections become experience
contribution: Uses failure recovery and feedback beyond pure imitation
limitations: Human/reset cost, reward misspecification, narrow task protocols
openness: Code and workflows available; hardware-specific integration required

name: MolmoAct2
inputs: Images, language, state
architecture: Molmo2-ER embodied reasoning backbone plus continuous flow-matching action expert
training: Molmo2-ER backbone -> discrete autoregressive MolmoAct2-Pretrain -> flow-matching action expert; MolmoAct2-Think is a separate depth-token-reasoning variant.
data: Released reasoning and robot training datasets, with embodiment-specific adaptation
inference: Closed-loop manipulation using conditioned action expert
contribution: Combines open embodied reasoning assets with continuous robot action learning
limitations: Reasoning metrics alone do not establish contact reliability; base checkpoints are not universal deployment policies
openness: Official code, models, staged checkpoints and dataset links

name: Xiaomi-Robotics-0
inputs: Multi-view images, instruction and proprioception
architecture: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct VLM plus diffusion transformer; 4.7B total per official page
training: Choice-policy VLM training; freeze VLM and train flow expert; prefix-conditioned post-training
data: Robot and vision-language mixtures plus task-specific teleoperation
inference: Buffered asynchronous chunks with committed prefix alignment
contribution: Treats deployment scheduling and action responsiveness as training-design issues
limitations: Requires matching async checkpoint, valid normalization, hardware adaptation and task data
openness: Code, weights and full post-training pipeline announced April 2026
